verdict.rationale: Anytype is local-first by default (data lives on-device) and offers explicit alternatives: local-only mode (no backup node at all) or self-hosting your own sync/backup node (with a maintained Docker image), giving users real control over where data physically resides rather than being locked to a vendor cloud region. This satisfies the spirit of data residency/sovereignty but there is no literal 'pick a region' selector for a managed cloud tier — control is achieved via local-only vs self-host vs Anytype's own network, not granular geographic choice. Missing for 10: a documented region-picker for the hosted/sync service, and independent confirmation that self-hosted deployments can be pinned to a specific geography.
